newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel rules out weakening EMU criteria.
newsitem.headline: Waigel rules out weakening EMU criteria.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Monday any weakening of the Maastricht deficit criteria for European monetary union would be irresponsible because it would send the wrong signals to financial markets.

Speaking in an interview with ZDF television, Waigel said he was already concerned about some countries using "creative accounting" in order to qualify for Maastricht's strict budget deficit limits of three percent of total government spending.

"There can be no expansion of the deficit horizon," Waigel said. "The three percent deficit limit is what is in the Maastricht Treaty and that is necessary, especially in face of the creative accounting being used in some countries.
"I consider it not responsible to accept any further compromises. It would give the markets the wrong signals."
Waigel said he was confident the German budget deficit would be well under three percent in 1997.
"We assume we have reliable data for next year and it looks like there is no danger," he said.
